title: Sierra Robotics outbound & research sketchbook
content:
Intro and purpose: Quick working notebook for outreach to Sierra Robotics (mid-market robotics integrator specializing in warehouse autonomous mobile robots). Goal: qualify partnership for an early access pilot of Redwood Private for on-prem inference workloads and a hosted API trial for cloud aggregation.

Account snapshot:
- HQ: Seattle, WA; ~220 employees; Series C (2023); customers: 3PLs, cold storage logistics
- Tech signal: open-source ROS-based fleet control, in-house vision models (PyTorch), mixed CPU/GPU inference - some on-edge Jetson devices, limited MLOps
- Recent news: announced "Sierra Dock" integration with ColdChainX (press release Oct 2025). Hiring: Senior ML Infra role opened Dec 2025 (indicates scaling infra needs)

Key stakeholders (mapping from LinkedIn + outreach threads):
- Priya Nair — Head of ML (decision driver for model infra)
- Marcos Vega — Director of Systems Engineering (influence on integration/ops)
- Jenna Park — VP of Product (use-case champion for robotics fleet features)
- Arun Patel — Platform Eng (day-to-day on infra, possible pilot contact)
- Sales contact: Tom Ellison (referred via partner X)

Hypothesis / why Redwood matters to them:
- Need predictable, low-latency on-prem inference for control loops and vision pipelines. Edge GPUs are capacity-constrained and ops overhead is high.
- Redwood Private can provide an audit-friendly, private control plane they can manage (appeals to security/compliance for cold storage clients).
- Routing/fallback features let them combine edge/cluster inference: cheap CPU fallback + cloud-hosted heavy ops for non-critical batch tasks.
- Cost profile predictable vs. building own serving stack; we can shorten time-to-pilot.

High-level outreach sequence (5 touchpoints):
1) Day 0 — intro email (short), mention mutual partner ColdChainX + lightweight value: "pilot to reduce inference ops by 40%" stat (internal estimate).
2) Day 4 — LinkedIn + one-pager with architecture sketch: edge + private control plane + canary routing.
3) Day 10 — product-teaser video + invite to 20-min tech readout (emphasize SLOs, canary rollout, rollback).
4) Day 18 — ROI note and cost modeling snapshot for their fleet (assumptions explicit). Offer free 30-day pilot with Redwood Dedicated credits.
5) Day 30 — last-play: internal case study ask or intro to partner ColdChainX for co-sell.

Draft cold email (short):
Subject: Quick pilot idea for Sierra Robotics + ColdChainX
Hi Priya —
I saw Sierra Dock's ColdChainX integration — congrats. Small idea: Redwood can run a short pilot (on-prem control plane + cloud fallback) to cut per-frame inference ops and operational toil. Typical win for similar customers: 30–50% reduction in ops cost and simpler rollback for model updates. 20 minutes to show what a pilot looks like?
— Ishaan (growth@redwood.ai)

Phone / demo script bullets (for initial intro call):
- Intro (30s): who we are, specific platform modes (Private, Dedicated, Hosted).
- Pain check (1–2 min): "How are you currently pushing model updates to edge fleets? How often do rollbacks happen?"
- Value props mapped: private control plane, deterministic latency, canaries + automatic fallback, cost controls (dedicated pools).
- Quick architecture sketch (2–3 min): edge devices -> local inference pool (optional) -> Redwood Private control plane -> cloud fallback models.
- Ask: 2-week technical spike + access to small dataset/sim logs for latency profiling.

Objections & rebuttals (working):
- "We already have an infra — building it is cheaper." -> Rebuttal: show TCO estimate comparing 9–12 months of eng time vs. pilot credits; plus ops cost for model updates and compliance overhead. Offer a scoped pilot to prove assumptions.
- "Data security concerns for cloud." -> Rebuttal: emphasize on-prem/private control plane, KMS integration, audit logs we can expose; propose an on-site demo under NDA.
- "Vendor lock-in worries." -> Rebuttal: highlight open-model friendly approach, ability to pin model versions and exportable configs; rollback and export procedures documented.
- "We run on Jetsons / edge only." -> Rebuttal: Redwood supports hybrid routing; propose edge caching + sparse cloud offload for heavy frames; demo latency profile from similar customers.

Prep checklist before technical spike (deliverables to request):
- Small sample of anonymized inference traces (500–2k frames)
- Current latency and throughput metrics per model (p50/p95/p99)
- A list of edge hardware models and available network topology between devices and datacenter
- Primary stakeholder time for 30-min design review

Success criteria for pilot (scoped):
- p95 inference latency reduction in critical pipeline or deterministic bound met
- Safe rollback exercised once without service interruption
- Cost delta assessed (ops + infra) vs. baseline
- Internal sign-off from ML lead to continue to MLP (proof-of-concept -> production)

Notes / questions to surface during first call:
- Is model training separate from serving? Who triggers new deploys?
- Are there regulatory/compliance constraints (customer-level)?
- Preferred telemetry and tracing formats (OTLP/Prometheus?)

Next steps (owner: Ishaan):
- Reach out to Priya via email + Tom (referrer) cc — draft queued in Outreach folder
- Create lightweight cost model (template: linked in Confluence-1283)
- Align with Solutions Eng (Lena) to book a 20-min tech readout in week of Jan 12

Misc scratch ideas:
- Offer a joint workshop with ColdChainX to show co-sell path
- Bring an example quantized model (4-bit) benchmark on Jetson to address perf skepticism
- If legal wants more, offer red team audit checklist and PoC NDA template
